curation.lead:
Sultan Ahmed Bin Sulayem, Chairman and Group CEO of DP World — Dubai's state-owned global port operator — maintained a close personal relationship with Jeffrey Epstein documented across 6,857 DOJ records spanning 2005 to 2018. Their correspondence reveals Epstein functioning not as a financial advisor but as something far more unusual: a back-channel diplomat and intelligence broker who connected a senior Emirati official with Israeli and British power structures at a time when the UAE had no formal diplomatic relations with Israel. Sulayem's emails repeatedly demonstrate that Epstein was his conduit to Ehud Barak, former Israeli Prime Minister; to Lord Peter Mandelson, UK Secretary of State; and to Tom Barrack, who would become chair of Trump's inaugural committee.

The operational depth of the relationship is extraordinary. Epstein ghostwrote Sulayem's official correspondence to the British government regarding an 800 million pound port project. He arranged Israeli medical treatment for Sulayem's entire family at Assaf Harofe Medical Center — complete with temporary hospital IDs for Sultan, his wife Istiqama Reimi, and their children Shamsa and Rashid. Barak facilitated Israeli visas for Sulayem, and Epstein arranged a three-month residence for the family at a Tel Aviv penthouse on Rothschild Boulevard. These are not the actions of a casual social acquaintance; they describe an intelligence-grade back-channel between a Gulf state official and the Israeli security establishment, with Epstein as the essential intermediary.

Perhaps most troublingly, Sulayem acted as an active participant in what investigators have termed Epstein's "placement pipeline." In June 2017, Sulayem personally emailed Fettah Tamince, chairman of the Rixos Hotels chain, to arrange a position at the Rixos Antalya spa for a Russian woman identified as "the personal masseuse at the private Spa of our friend Jeffery Epstien." Sulayem forwarded the woman's Russian passport directly. This intervention — a senior UAE government official placing one of Epstein's staff into a third party's hotel operation — implicates Sulayem not merely as a beneficiary of Epstein's services but as an operational node who facilitated the movement of women across international borders within Epstein's network.

Did Deutsche Bank flag Sulayem's PEP status in connection with Epstein's accounts, and were any Suspicious Activity Reports filed related to transactions between or involving both parties?

What was the purpose of 30 23andMe DNA kits ordered under the alias James Miller — were they actually distributed to DP World employees, or did they serve Epstein's documented interest in collecting genetic data on associates and their networks?

What is the full scope of the Sulayem-Tamince-Epstein triangle, and were there other instances of women being placed into Rixos Hotels facilities through this channel beyond the documented June 2017 episode?

What triggered Sulayem's period of apparent "exile" referenced by Tom Barrack in October 2010, and how did Epstein's continued support during this period create obligations that deepened Sulayem's dependence on the relationship?

Who were the unnamed people Epstein sent to Sulayem in Dubai that prompted the response "thank you, they are a treasure, no girl in dubai is safe tonite," and what was the actual nature of their visit?

Did Sulayem attend the March 2018 dinner at 9 East 71st Street with Steve Bannon and Ehud Barak, and what was the purpose of assembling a former Israeli PM, a former White House strategist, and a UAE port chairman at Epstein's residence?

sections.title: The UAE-Israel Back-Channel
sections.content:
The central significance of Sultan Bin Sulayem in the Epstein network is what his relationship reveals about Epstein's role as a private diplomatic back-channel between the UAE and Israel — two countries that, throughout most of the documented period, had no formal diplomatic relations. The Abraham Accords normalizing UAE-Israel ties were not signed until September 2020, yet the Sulayem-Barak-Epstein channel was operational at least five years earlier.

The channel began taking shape at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) in June 2015, where Ehud Barak — Israel's former Prime Minister and Defense Minister — met Sulayem in person. Barak's debriefing email to Epstein, titled "Fwd: Touch Base SS," addresses Sulayem with the Arabic honorific "Khadrat El Sultan" and reports that "SS" expressed interest in "finding some area for actual cooperation." Epstein had orchestrated the meeting. The same SPIEF trip saw Barak meeting Russian Central Bank Governor Nabiulina, Foreign Minister Lavrov, former Finance Minister Kudrin, VTB chief Kostin, and Sberbank chief Gref — a roster that demonstrates the caliber of access Epstein could deliver.

By July 2018, the back-channel had matured into a fully operational relationship. Sulayem emailed Barak directly: "Dear Ehud, This is Sultan bin sulayem we were introduced by Jeffrey and we met at the st Petersburg forum a few times first of all I want to thank you for your help with our visa I am in Tell Aviv since July 3rd." The visa assistance from a former Israeli Prime Minister to a sitting UAE government official is a diplomatic act that would have been impossible through official channels. Barak's wife Nili Priell arranged housing — a three-bedroom Tel Aviv penthouse at 1 Rothschild Boulevard — where Sulayem's family stayed for three months from July through October 2018. During this period, Sulayem's entire family received medical treatment at Assaf Harofe Medical Center with temporary patient IDs, an arrangement coordinated by Epstein through his jeevacation@gmail.com and jeeproject@yahoo.com addresses. Epstein vouched for Sulayem to the hospital: "thx, he is a very good guy."

sections.title: DP World and Political Door-Opening
sections.content:
Sulayem's professional position made him a high-value contact for Epstein's network. As Chairman and Group CEO of DP World — a Dubai state-owned company that operates 78 marine terminals and inland terminals across six continents — and Chairman of its parent Dubai World, Sulayem sat at a critical intersection of Gulf state power and global trade infrastructure. DP World's operations touch over 40 countries, making Sulayem a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) whose associations carried enhanced regulatory scrutiny obligations for any financial institution involved — a status that Deutsche Bank apparently failed to flag in its Epstein account compliance reviews.

The most concrete evidence of Epstein's role as Sulayem's political fixer is the London Gateway Port correspondence. In November 2009, Sulayem — as DP World Chairman — drafted a formal letter to Lord Mandelson, then UK Secretary of State for Business, seeking British government financial guarantees for the London Gateway Port and Park project, valued at 672 million pounds in its first phase alone. Before sending the letter, Sulayem forwarded it to Epstein with the note: "Dear Jeffrey I am sending this to Peter in the next 20 mnts." The casual first-name reference to a sitting British cabinet minister, routed through a convicted sex offender, reveals the nature of the channel: Epstein had introduced Sulayem to Mandelson and continued to function as the intermediary for a major infrastructure deal between Dubai and the United Kingdom. The letter was sent ahead of a state visit by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai — placing Epstein's facilitation role at the level of sovereign diplomacy.

Epstein's corporate connection to Sulayem also involved Jide Zeitlin, whose documented link to Sulayem through EFTA02453039 suggests an additional corporate or advisory relationship that has not yet been fully traced.

sections.title: The Placement Pipeline and Suggestive Communications
sections.content:
The most disturbing aspect of the Sulayem dossier is his documented role in facilitating the movement of women connected to Epstein. On June 5, 2017, Sulayem directly emailed Fettah Tamince, Chairman of Rixos Hotels, regarding a Russian woman: "She works as the personal masseuse at the private Spa of our friend Jeffery Epstien. I would appreciate if you can arrange for her to work as a trainee at Rixos Antalia spa so she gains better experiences." Tamince replied immediately: "Dear sultan I will make sure asap." The woman, who held a Russian passport, wrote separately that she was "ready to go as soon as possible." Sulayem forwarded her passport documentation to facilitate the arrangement.

The transaction is significant on multiple levels. A senior UAE government official personally intervened with a Turkish hotel magnate to place one of Epstein's staff members in an overseas spa facility. The speed and casualness of the exchange — Tamince's instant "I will make sure asap" — suggests this was not an unusual request within their relationship. The involvement of a Russian national with access to Epstein's private spa, being moved into a Turkish resort chain, traces a cross-border pipeline for women that operated through Epstein's Gulf and Turkish contacts.

Earlier communications are more cryptic but no less concerning. In a message documented in EFTA02465174, after Epstein had apparently sent people to visit Sulayem in Dubai, Sulayem responded: "thank you, they are a treasure, no girl in dubai is safe tonite." The exact context is unclear, but the language is highly suggestive and consistent with patterns documented across Epstein's broader network. Separately, in April 2016, Epstein responded to an unnamed photo sent by Sulayem with the same phrase — "no girl in dubai is safe tonite" — suggesting an established pattern of communication about women between the two men.

sections.title: SPIEF and the Russian Dimension
sections.content:
Sulayem's appearances at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) connect him to the Russian dimension of Epstein's operations. At SPIEF 2015, Barak — reporting to Epstein — described meetings with the most senior figures in Russian state finance: Central Bank Governor Elvira Nabiulina, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, former Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin, VTB Bank chief Andrey Kostin, and Sberbank chief German Gref. Also present were Baroness Rothschild, Lord Mandelson, and "senior people from David's branch of the Rothschild family." Putin himself was interviewed by Charlie Rose at the forum with former heads of state in attendance.

The forum organizer, Sergey Belyakov, maintained a documented connection to Sulayem. Barak's report to Epstein carefully distinguished between "Sergey" (Belyakov, the organizer) and "SS" (Sulayem), noting that SS "expressed interest in finding some area for actual cooperation." Sulayem later paneled alongside Mandelson at SPIEF, extending his presence at the forum beyond a single year. This positions Sulayem as a recurring participant in a venue that served as Epstein's primary interface with Russian state power.

The connection between Tom Barrack and Sulayem adds an American political dimension. When Epstein asked Barrack in October 2010, "paris will you see sultan?," Barrack replied: "I did. He is in exile quite sad." The reference to exile suggests Sulayem experienced a period of political difficulty — likely connected to the 2009 Dubai World debt crisis, when the company sought to restructure billion in debt. By August 2011, Barrack reported the relationship had recovered: "Just saw Sultan who likes you a lot! I told him you are the best." In January 2017, Sulayem consulted Epstein about whether to accept Barrack's invitation to Trump's inauguration — a decision that carried diplomatic implications for a senior UAE official.

sections.title: DNA Kits and Surveillance Patterns
sections.content:
Two episodes in the Sulayem correspondence align with Epstein's documented interest in collecting biological and personal data on associates. In 2015, Epstein ordered 30 23andMe Ancestry Personal Genetic Service kits totaling $3,151.95, billed under the alias "James Miller" via PayPal and shipped to a UAE address for Sulayem. Sulayem requested that all 30 kits be registered under a single name. When the order was repeated in May-June 2017 — this time shipped to Epstein's residence at 9 East 71st Street — the bulk purchase triggered a compliance review by 23andMe. Epstein's staff intervened with customer service, explaining that Sulayem "would like to give them to his co-workers so they too may enjoy investigating their ancestry. Sultan participated with his own DNA and found it fascinating."

The ostensible explanation is plausible on its surface, but the details are unusual. Thirty DNA kits distributed from a single registration point, ordered through an alias, with Epstein's direct involvement in resolving a compliance flag — this pattern is consistent with Epstein's documented interest in genetic data collection across his network. Whether the kits were used as described or served some other purpose in Epstein's data-gathering operations remains an open question.

Sulayem's broader communication patterns also reveal the intimacy and operational nature of the relationship. He shared his real-time location with Epstein via Apple Maps pins from locations including Gambia and Geneva. He sent Epstein aircraft comparison documents in June 2013, suggesting they discussed private aviation. He asked Epstein to purchase a "death watch" countdown clock from Amazon, specifying it should count past 2050. These details describe a relationship of unusual personal closeness and mutual trust between a senior Gulf state official and an American financier who was, by this point, a registered sex offender.
